title: Choose the visual world — Affey for Governor (second hand)
question: The roll assigned The Envoy's Passport. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. All directions use only the locked palette.

options.label: The Envoy's Passport
options.lineage: A well-travelled diplomat's passport: the portrait page, security-ruled paper, and dated entry stamps from every posting, ending at home
options.thesis: The record told as a passport: a portrait page opens the site, and each milestone is a dated stamp on the way back to Wajir.
options.viewport: A sand portrait page set on the green cover: photo left, the name in a large engraved serif, the promise, Donate; a stamp for 1997; the countdown runs along the foot like a printed date strip.
options.risk: Must stay a generic passport grammar (no national emblem, no machine-readable code) to avoid looking like an official document; stamps can turn gimmicky if overused.

raised.raise: Total ink commitment: every photograph is printed in the palette's two inks (green and ochre duotone), never in raw colour beside them.
The timeline always shows where 'now' is: one marker on the record line between 1997 and 10 August 2027.
One strict grid carries every page; captions and dates live inside it, never floating.
Milestones sit in one ranked row read in order, with a single fixed format per stamp.
Each page is a measured sequence of reveals along one axis, so scrolling feels walked, not stacked.

options.label: The Wajir Horizon
options.lineage: The low, wide horizon of Wajir's plains, where the sky takes most of the frame
options.thesis: Every page hangs off one horizon line: the sky field above holds the headline, the land below holds the facts and actions.
options.viewport: The name in a huge serif across a quiet sky field; the promise sits on the horizon line; below it, land in green-ochre duotone carries Donate and the day count.
options.risk: The landscape-hero is a familiar campaign move, and it leans on real Wajir photography the campaign does not have yet.

options.label: Campaign Broadside Train
options.thesis: Each section is a railcar broadside: stencil capitals, photomontage and a red wedge that drives the action.
options.viewport: A diagonal wedge carries Donate into a photomontage of the candidate with the promise stencilled along the line of travel.
options.case: Holds product clarity (the action literally drives the page) but loses audience identification: its revolutionary-propaganda lineage and aggression clash with a statesman's restraint.
options.risk: Reads as agitation rather than gravitas; diagonals cost legibility in Somali and Swahili.

options.label: Fluorescent Tech Spread
options.thesis: Two fluorescent inks for absolutely everything.
options.viewport: An angled headline slab over a duotone photo.
options.risk: Impossible inks break the locked palette.

options.label: Rhythm Machine Step Row
options.thesis: Sixteen step keys under a running chase light.
options.viewport: A step row as the page's timeline.
options.risk: A music toy for a governor's campaign.
options.kept: The timeline always shows where now is.

options.label: ASCII Live Render
options.thesis: Glyph density stands in for light.
options.risk: Unreadable as a portrait; heavy canvas work on mid-range phones.

options.label: Glaze-Run Kiln Shelf
options.thesis: Glazes pool, run and fuse on a kiln shelf.
options.viewport: A ranked shelf of glazed cups.
options.risk: Cobalt is outside the locked palette; no link to Wajir.
options.kept: One ranked row with one fixed format per item.

options.label: Versailles Vistas
options.thesis: Axial vistas that break into hidden green rooms.
options.viewport: A palace terrace looking down one axis.
options.risk: European palace grandeur is the wrong symbol for Wajir.
options.kept: A measured sequence of reveals along one axis.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A full-bleed candidate portrait with a bold sans headline, pill buttons and card sections, executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Portrait fills the screen behind a dark gradient; name, promise and two buttons bottom-left.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other campaign site by design.
